_comment: MODELED scenario (not a measured run). Open-source GitHub issue triage. Public-data-friendly, domain-neutral. Assumptions documented in README.md. Replace with measured values from a real triage pilot to make this a primary-source case study.
task_description: Triage one incoming open-source GitHub issue: classify, detect duplicates, estimate severity, suggest next step, draft maintainer response
model: frontier LLM + embedding search over existing issues (modeled)

value._comment: Deliverable value = value of one correctly-triaged issue (routed, labeled, contributor engaged so it can be resolved). AI version marginally higher from faster first response. See README sensitivity note.

cost_baseline._comment: Maintainer at a senior-engineer loaded rate. 12 min/issue. Risk = expected cost of misrouting/mislabeling (~downstream rework).

cost_ai._comment: AI classifies, runs embedding search for duplicates, estimates severity, drafts the response; maintainer verifies. Risk is HIGHER than baseline ($8 vs $5): a bad auto-response can alienate a contributor — a real community cost, only partly offset by verification.

validation._comment: Maintainer accepts ~82% of AI labels/drafts as-is; 18% edited. All triaged issues are acted on.

overuse_benchmark.benchmark_description: Smaller classification model + cached embeddings reaches comparable triage quality at M=$0.02

notes: Modeled from plausible OSS maintainer economics. NOT a measured pilot. Public GitHub issues make this fully reproducible with real data.
